subject: science
domain: Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer

items.prompt:
Which wave is used to transmit information?
A) Radio waves
B) No waves
C) Only sound in a room
D) Only water waves

Fiber-optic cables carry data using
A) light waves
B) sound waves only
C) water waves
D) no waves

A camera captures an image using
A) light waves
B) sound waves
C) water waves
D) no waves

Cell phones communicate using
A) radio and microwave signals
B) only wires
C) only light bulbs
D) sound in the air only

steps: Cell phones use radio and microwave signals.

items.prompt:
Information is carried on a wave as
A) a pattern the wave carries
B) a solid object
C) a liquid
D) nothing
items.answer: A) a pattern the wave carries

steps: Information is encoded as a pattern.

items.prompt:
Waves are useful for sending information far because they
A) travel fast and over long distances
B) move very slowly
C) cannot leave a room
D) carry nothing
items.answer: A) travel fast and over long distances

items.prompt:
A message can reach the other side of the world almost instantly because
A) waves carrying the information travel very fast over long distances
B) messages teleport
C) waves move slowly
D) nothing carries it
items.answer: A) waves carrying the information travel very fast over long distances

steps: Fast waves carry the message quickly.

items.prompt:
Which best communicates how waves transmit a message worldwide?
A) The message becomes a pattern carried by radio, microwave, or light waves and is read back at the other end
B) The message walks there
C) Waves cannot carry messages
D) Only wires work
items.answer: A) The message becomes a pattern carried by radio, microwave, or light waves and is read back at the other end

steps: Waves carry the encoded message far and fast.
